title: What You Do After Easter Matters — John 21:15
paragraphs: What You Do After Easter Matters — John 21:15
He rose.
But what do you do the morning after the miracle?
In John 21:15, the risen Jesus does not first ask Peter about power, gifting, or platform. He asks one piercing question: “Do you love Me?” Then He gives one clear command: “Feed My lambs.”
That is the weight of Easter.

Not just celebrating an empty tomb.
Not just feeling inspired for one Sunday.
Not just posting “He is risen” and going back to your old chains.

Easter is not only proof that Jesus conquered death.
It is a call to love Him enough to obey Him.

Peter had failed publicly.
He denied Jesus three times.
Shame should have been the end of his story.

But beside another fire, Jesus did not crush him.
Jesus restored him.
And that is where grace walks in.
The risen Christ meets broken people, not to leave them broken, but to recommission them. The cross paid for Peter’s sin. The resurrection secured Peter’s future. And now love had to become action.

That is the question for us too:
After Easter, will you drift back to comfort?
Or will you follow the Savior you say you love?
Because what you do after Easter matters.

If Jesus is alive, then repentance cannot be delayed.
Forgiveness cannot be treated lightly.
Calling cannot stay buried.
And love for Christ must show up in the way we live, serve, and shepherd others.

Some people want resurrection power without surrendered hearts.
But Jesus still asks,
“Do you love Me?”

Not, “Do you admire Me?”
Not, “Do you agree with Me?”
Not, “Do you post about Me?”
But, “Do you love Me?”

Real love feeds His sheep.
Real love returns after failure.
Real love follows Jesus all the way.

And here is the hope:
Peter was not restored because he was strong.
He was restored because Jesus is merciful.
That same mercy is for you.

If you have failed, come back.
If you have gone cold, come back.
If shame has been preaching louder than grace, come back.

The empty tomb means your worst moment does not get the final word.
Jesus does.

Prayer:
Lord Jesus, after Easter, keep me from empty religion and shallow emotion. Teach me to love You truly, repent deeply, and follow You fully. Restore what failure tried to ruin, and make my life a testimony of Your grace. Amen.
